UPDATE with bill text - Proposed House bill would amend Controlled Substances Act to follow state laws on marijuana, effectively ending federal enforcement of the drug war

Well, no, this isn't going to end the drug war. It's definitely a step in the right direction, though.

Right now, federal law trumps state law in regards to medical marijuana (MMJ). MMJ is still on Schedule 1, which is defined as a substance with absolutely no medical value whatsoever. Heroin and cocaine are also on Schedule 1. Federal law makes it illegal to sell any Schedule 1 substances. This bill would only prevent the federal government from prosecuting people under the Schedule 1 restrictions for marijuana violations in states with MMJ laws. It doesn't remove MMJ from Schedule 1, nor does it change any of the draconian minimum sentencing laws that keep so many people incarcerated in for-profit prisons, nor does it do anything to discourage law enforcement from sending non-MMJ drug possessors to said prisons. It also doesn't address the state prosecutors who, despite the will of the people being in favor of MMJ, continue to arrest and charge people with possession in states with MMJ laws. (Source: I live in one such state.)

The drug war is big business, especially for the growing private prison industry. To truly end the drug war, both the fat-cat corporate criminals and the organized street criminals (i.e, the mob) must be dealt with; that's a whole lotta money people stand to lose, so you can bet they're gonna fight tooth and nail to keep it.

The students are definitely in the right on this one.

For the first reason, being that such a dress code way too ridiculously specific. These are college students, not adults in the workforce who have had time to reasonably acquire a fully stocked wardrobe. How could they reasonably expect a good turnout at such an event if they planned to enforce such a strict dress code so closely? What about the people who didn't have every single item on that list?

For the second reason being that what they require them to wear isn't even the correct thing to wear to a job interview. INnfact, they got it exactly backwards. A black suit is never appropriate for a job interview, it's only appropriate for a black tie event, only to be worn after 6, or in the event of a funeral. Gray suits with solid white shirts and solid ties border on being appropriate, but only for the most formal of job interviews. Maybe the IRS or a hugely bureaucratic company, but nothing less formal than that.

Navy suits, with white or light blue shirts with a subtle pattern on them with a tie that complements those colors, on the other hand, is about as perfect a job interview outfit as you can put together. You can wear it with black or brown lace up oxfords, with a matching leather belt, and the suit works in basically every season. Blue as a color also conveys trustworthiness, which is what you want to be presenting in an interview.

TL;DR, Rutgers was wrong, Blue suits are the way to go.
